title: Capital One — the cloud engineer who bragged

scenes.narration: [serious] A hacker's bragging online exposed data on 100 million Americans.
Capital One is a big American bank. It kept customer data on Amazon's rented computers.
In March 2019, someone slipped past a badly set security gate.
Then the data was copied. 100 million Americans and 6 million Canadians. Including 140,000 secret ID numbers.
Later, a stranger warned the bank. Some of the data was posted on a public code website.
The FBI tracked the posts to Paige Thompson, a former Amazon worker.
In 2022, a jury found her guilty. Her own bragging was the clue.

facts.claim: About 100 million people in the U.S. and 6 million in Canada were affected, including about 140,000 Social Security numbers and 80,000 bank account numbers, mostly from credit card applications from 2005 to 2019; the intrusion happened March 22-23, 2019 through a misconfigured web application firewall
FBI agents tied together Thompson's postings on GitHub, Slack and Twitter; she was a former Amazon Web Services employee and Capital One is an AWS customer
Capital One found the vulnerability on July 19, 2019, two days after an email told it some of its data had appeared on GitHub

A Seattle jury convicted Thompson in June 2022 of wire fraud, unauthorized access to a protected computer and damaging a protected computer; she was sentenced to time served plus five years of probation; she was arrested in July 2019
The Treasury Department fined Capital One $80 million for failing to protect the data
